## Verdict

Acme Desk costs least for a team of 35, at $280 per month. Its 10-seat minimum sits well below the team size, so all 35 seats bill at the $8 list rate with nothing wasted. Kelp is the most expensive at $850, driven as much by its 50-seat floor as by its headline price.

## Vendors

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $8 | 10 |
| Fennel HQ | $12 | 25 |
| Kelp | $17 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (35) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Acme Desk:** minimum 10 is below 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $8 = **$280 per month**.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 25 is below 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $12 = **$420 per month**.
- **Kelp:** minimum 50 exceeds 35, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $17 = **$850 per month**. Fifteen seats, worth $255, go unused.

Acme Desk is $140 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ and $570 cheaper than Kelp — $1,680 and $6,840 over twelve months.

## Risks

Kelp's position is partly an artefact of its minimum. Its effective rate at 35 people is $24.29 per person ($850 ÷ 35), falling to $17 once the team reaches 50. Even then it remains the dearest per seat, so the ranking holds at any size on this list.

The price list gives per-seat rates and minimums and nothing else. Feature coverage, support tiers, security posture, usage limits and integrations are all unknown here, so this says which vendor is cheapest, not which is the better buy.

All figures assume monthly billing at list price, as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding fees and overage charges are not in the source and could reorder these totals. Worth confirming whether Kelp's 50-seat floor is negotiable at 35 people before ruling it out on price alone.
